source.prompt: What is the best CRM for a solo founder just starting out?
source.note: real collected answer; brand, competitors and publishers are the specs the cycle was scored with

answer.text:
There is no single "best" CRM for a solo founder—it depends entirely on what you sell and how you run your business. 

As a solo founder, your biggest bottleneck is **time**. Spending hours configuring or logging data into a complex CRM takes away from building and closing deals. 

---

### **The Top CRMs by Founder Archetype**

| CRM | Best For | Pros | Cons / Catch | Starting Price |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **HubSpot** | **Product / SaaS / Content Founders** | Excellent free plan, top-notch UI, strong inbound marketing tools & forms. | Paid tiers escalate drastically (e.g., $100+/mo) once you outgrow free features. | **Free** |
| **Pipedrive** | **B2B / Service Founders with High Deal Volume** | Best visual drag-and-drop pipeline, clear activity tracking. | Weak on long-term contact networking; built purely for closing deals. | **~$14–$24/mo** |
| **Streak** | **Founders Who Live in Gmail** | Lives directly inside your Gmail inbox; zero context switching. | Tied strictly to Google Workspace; limited mobile reporting. | **Free** tier available |
| **folk** | **Relationship-First & Network-Led Founders** | Contact-centric, great LinkedIn Chrome extension, seamless email sequences. | Less ideal if you need heavy automated sales pipelines or complex reporting. | **~$20/mo** |
| **Bigin (by Zoho)** | **Budget-Conscious Founders** | Extremely cheap, lightweight pipeline management, mobile-friendly. | Doesn't integrate deeply with complex cold outreach tools. | **Free** or ~$7/mo |

---

### **How to Decide**

* **If your budget is $0:** Start with **HubSpot Free**. It gives you contact tracking, meeting scheduling, and basic deal pipelines out of the box with no financial commitment.
* **If you spend all day sending emails:** Use **Streak** or **Salesflare**. They auto-log interactions directly from your inbox so you never have to manually enter contacts.
* **If you are pitching investors, advisors, and agency clients:** Use **folk** or **Notion**. They prioritize relationships and contact lists over traditional "deal stages".
* **If you run cold outreach or standard B2B sales:** Use **Pipedrive**. The UI is built specifically to remind you of your next action so deals never slip through the cracks.

---

**Rule of Thumb:** If you have under 10 active leads, even a clean **Notion CRM template** or **Google Sheet** is better than over-engineering your stack. Move to a dedicated tool only when manual tracking causes dropped follow-ups.
